location_name: Continental shelf north of the Natuna Islands (Indonesia-South Vietnam overlap, Agip contract area)
summary: At informal technical talks with South Vietnam in Saigon on 22 June 1972, Indonesian negotiators insisted that the continental-shelf boundary be an equidistance line drawn from the outermost islands (the Natuna group) and, according to a later Indonesian Ministry of Mining letter, their presentation simultaneously constituted a protest against South Vietnam's entry, under its June 1971 concession decree, into Indonesian shelf already contracted by Pertamina to Agip.
